statement: For a simply connected spherical domain with nondegenerate locally connected frontier, the actual Carathéodory quotient identifies the boundary-fixed closed-disk group with the orientation-preserving sphere group fixing the complement; the full relative group is contractible. For a closed-disk operator group whose actual interior restriction closure acts freely and properly and contains a specified closed-disk conjugate of a torsion-free first-kind Fuchsian group, restriction identifies its boundary-fixed centralizer with the entire interior centralizer as topological groups. Every based loop in that relative centralizer has a based equivariant filling. This applies through the original prime-end quotient even when its boundary fibers are nontrivial, retaining all operator labels and the specified plane infinity outside the domain.
depends_on: C67 actual Carathéodory quotient and prime-end functor; proved nonconstant-arc and unlinked-fiber argument; Jordan separation; C26/C30 verified Polish open orbit-map theorem; Tukia 1972 Section 3.B, Proposition 3.5 and Corollary 3.5.1; C33 proper-action injection; C66 one-end topology comparison
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and relative frontier extension
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The original Tukia proof was read in full at the cited passage. The first-kind action is required through a specified homeomorphism of the closed disk and an actual subgroup inclusion into the original restriction closure. No arbitrary interior uniformization is assumed to extend to the original prime-end circle. The spherical quotient is not assumed injective on its boundary.
notes: Alternating pairs in two distinct Carathéodory boundary fibers would give a Jordan curve whose two complementary sides approach the same different frontier point, a contradiction. Together with absence of constant boundary arcs, this forces every orientation-preserving boundary map u with q u=q to be identity, including slit and slender locally connected frontiers. Compact quotient descent and the Polish open mapping argument prove the exact spherical group topology. Tukia extends each actual interior centralizer element for the specified first-kind subgroup; its boundary map is identity. Restriction between the two closed Polish centralizers is therefore a continuous bijective homomorphism and hence a topological isomorphism. C33 fills the interior loop, and the continuous inverse extends the whole filling and its inverse family to the fixed frontier. Alexander contraction is used only in the full relative disk group to verify ambient nullity. No finite-generation or cocompactness hypothesis is imposed on the first-kind subgroup, and no general boundary-restriction fibration or infinite-component pasting is claimed. C12 remains open.
